title: Entertainers Cafe, Louisville and Royal Gardens; Manuel Perez
summary: They recap leaving the Entertainers Cafe for Louisville, then Dreamland and Royal Gardens, and a trumpeter relative who went back to New Orleans, probably Manuel Perez.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: The Wickliffe band, when you joined them, was where?
Now, did you leave Entertainers when they closed it down for Prohibition, or for Padlocked or something like that?
I think, I think so. Oh, I think that's the time I told you we went to Louisville.
You got a book in Louisville for a month.

And we were in Louisville for a month or five weeks. And we came back here. And then we, I think, I don't know if it's the exact time that Joe Oliver left and went to California. He left the old dream on that 35th Street. It was a colored dream on that 35th Street. And we went in there. And we stayed there. No, that was after we came from Milwaukee. From Milwaukee, we went to the, the, the dreamland. And then, I think, Joe Oliver and them, they came back to the Royal Gardens on 31st Street. And I think they either went into Waterville or they went back to the coast. Then we went, the Wickers band went into the Royal Gardens. And that's the trumpet player. I was trying to tell you, we had an awful good trumpet player in there. He might have been Kepard. He might have been Kepard, yeah. I'm trying to think. I can't remember. He went back to New Orleans. Incidentally, he was, my mother, one of my relatives' cousins, Manuel. Manuel is in Spanish. Did he ever come north again? I don't know. I don't think so.
Theo went back. He didn't want to be anything in the north.
The weather. The boys never liked the weather. The weather's bad.
They speak of Perez as if he was mainly a good first man.
I think so, yes. Yes, that's right. Uh-huh.
